reason: I'd probably install the free 14-day trial since there's no auto-charge, but I wouldn't pay yet. A brand-new app with no ratings, guessing when I fell asleep from my phone lying next to me while I've got earphones in, isn't proof I'd trust. It's the app grading its own homework.
objection: How accurate is a phone on the nightstand at telling when I actually fell asleep or woke up? If the measurement is shaky, the 'it worked for you' chart at day 14 means nothing, and the refund depends on that same chart.
would_change_my_mind: Solid app-store ratings or an independent test showing the phone's sleep-onset detection matches a watch or sleep tracker, and then my own 14-day result showing a clear difference.
